newsitem.title: UK: UK's Carlton plans to expand in pay TV.
newsitem.headline: UK's Carlton plans to expand in pay TV.

text.p: British media company Carlton Communications Plc, the largest commercial television (ITV) operator, said on Wednesday it planned to expand in the growing pay TV market.

"We want to build up our interests in pay television, both as a content provider and operator. These may encompass cable, satellite and digital television," chairman Michael Green said in a statement. Carlton's pre-tax profit for the year ending September 30 rose 20 percent to 295.1 million pounds ($492.2 million).
Green said that Carlton was interested in digital terrestrial television, which is scheduled to begin in Britain in mid-1998.

"Digital terrestrial television will expand free-to-air broadcasting in the UK and opens the door to the establishment of further pay television services. We are examining these investment opportunities very carefully," he said.

Carlton operates the ITV licences for the English Midlands and London's weekday television and last month agreed to pay 85 million pounds ($141.8 million) to acquire Westcountry TV, which broadcasts to the south-western corner of England.

"Our business mix has produced solid growth over the last five years and, combined with the investments now being made, will continue to fuel Carlton's expansion...I look forward to the year ahead with confidence and enthusiasm," Green added. ($1=.5995 Pound)
